The regex is matching both the sidebar "All Encounters" link and another card with "All" in its name. I'll tighten the locator and check for the same pattern elsewhere.
The regex is also matching a dashboard card whose accessible name includes “All”. I’ll pin the click to the sidebar’s exact “All Encounters” link.

The regex `/all encounters/i` was matching two links that go to the same URL:

1. The sidebar item, accessible name **All Encounters**
2. A facility card whose name includes the same words (Playwright reported it as **Stethoscope Duo All**)

Playwright’s strict mode requires a single match, so the click failed.

The helper now uses the exact sidebar label:

```25:27:tests/organization/patient/helpers.ts
  await page
    .getByRole("link", { name: "All Encounters", exact: true })
    .click();
```

That uniquely targets the sidebar link. This is what `navigateToOrganizationPatient` uses, so both organization encounter specs should pass.

The observation-definition timeout on `meq/g` is a separate failure, not this locator. I can look at that next if you want.

is it regex that broke ?

Yes — the **loose regex** is what made Playwright see two matches. The new second link is why it started failing.

**What it is:** `{ name: /all encounters/i }` means “any link whose accessible name *contains* those words,” not “the link whose name is exactly All Encounters.”

**How it works here:** after Patients is opened, two links both include those words:

| Link | Accessible name | Matches `/all encounters/i`? | Matches `"All Encounters", exact: true`? |
|---|---|---|---|
| Sidebar | `All Encounters` | yes | yes |
| Overview card | `Stethoscope Duo All Encounters` (icon + label) | yes | no |

Playwright’s **strict mode** allows only one match, so `.click()` throws.

**Takeaway:** the extra card didn’t break the click by existing. The regex was too wide, so it matched the card too. Exact name is the right selector for the sidebar item.
